label: Second copy step (recalling orig token 1), strongest when an early original token is a
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and almost only at step L+1 (recall_idx == 1: the input is the fed-back first original token and the output is original token 1). That one step holds 97% of activation mass. Within it the firing rate is about 11%. It goes up with sequence length (rate rises from ~0 at L=3 to its highest at L=9) and goes up a lot when the letter a is among the next few original tokens: out_tok or next_out == a gives 13x lift, and all top examples look like x a a a ... Precision is incomplete. a at positions 1-3 gives precision ~0.59 and recall ~0.48 (dev). Long sequences without a and outputs such as o/p/f/q/c/y explain much of the remaining weak activation. Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, at recall_idx 0, or at recall_idx >= 3, and only weakly at recall_idx 2.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & out_tok=a (+4.51), orig3=a (+4.17), orig2=a (+3.92), recall_idx=1 (+3.81), prev_tok=<DEL> (+3.81), next_out=a (+2.86). Lower it: to_go=1 (-5.96), orig2=h (-5.50), phase=2 & out_tok=h (-4.96), in_first=1 (-4.81).
